decidedBy: the lead, 2026-10-08, on the family relationships that still contradicted themselves after batch K (PRB-0985, PRB-0986): each word read against its verse by an agent; no person has reviewed these rulings
policy: A word names the man its verse and its list name. Where the written spelling is a variant of a name the parallel passage and the order of the list show, the word names the man the list shows.
source: Essenthos, the family relationships left over from the kinship contradictions, read against their verses on 2026-10-08

rulings.why: 'And these are the children of Dishan; Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran': the Hebrew writes דִישָׁן, Dishan, here, but the verse stands in the list of Seir's sons where Dishon comes (Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, Dishan, GEN 36:20-28), 1 Chronicles 1:41 gives the same children as 'the sons of Dishon', and Brenton's Septuagint (Δησών) and the King James read Dishon. Dishan's own children are Uz and Aran (GEN 36:28). The word names Seir's son Dishon.

create.name: Azariah
create.distinguisher: son of Zadok the priest, one of Solomon's princes (1KI 4:2)
create.notes: Whether he is the Azariah son of Ahimaaz of 1CH 6:9 the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'And these were the princes which he had; Azariah the son of Zadok the priest' (עֲזַרְיָהוּ בֶן־צָדוֹק הַכֹּהֵן): 1CH 6:8-10 makes the Azariah son of Johanan Zadok's great-great-grandson, so the Azariah whose father is Zadok is not he; whether he is the son of Ahimaaz (1CH 6:9), Zadok's grandson, the passages do not say.
